name: End Users (Developers)
description: Individuals who authorize the agent to access Github on their behalf

name: Organization Owners
description: Administrators responsible for GitHub organizations whose repos may be managed by the agent

name: Repository Maintainers
description: People who manage repository health, triage, and merging

name: Collaborators/Contributors
description: Users with write access who contribute code and content

name: Project Managers/Product Owners
description: Plan and prioritize work reflected in issues and PRs the agent creates or summarizes

name: Security Engineers/Application Security
description: Oversee secure coding and secrets hygiene related to agent actions

name: Compliance Officers
description: Ensure the agent’s activities comply with internal policies and external standards

name: Privacy/Data Protection Officers
description: Oversee handling of private repo data and any personal data in issues/PRs

name: Risk Management/Governance
description: Assess and mitigate operational and technology risks of autonomous changes

name: Open-Source Community Maintainers
description: OSS maintainers impacted by agent-authored issues/PRs

name: Issue Reporters
description: Users who create issues that the agent reads, summarizes, or responds to

name: Pull Request Authors
description: Contributors whose PRs the agent summarizes, reviews, approves, or merges

name: Downstream Dependents
description: Projects and services relying on repos the agent modifies

name: Upstream Project Maintainers
description: Owners of dependencies influenced by agent-proposed fixes or changes

name: End Users/Customers of the Software
description: People using products built from repos affected by agent changes

name: Data Scientists/ML Engineers (Repo Authors)
description: Owners of notebooks/models the agent may run or modify

name: Students/Educators
description: Use the agent for learning and coursework on GitHub repositories

name: GitHub (Platform Provider)
description: API and service provider whose policies and availability affect the agent

name: GitHub Organization Administrators
description: Configure permissions, SSO, and app/scopes for agent access

name: OAuth/App Authorization Administrators
description: Approve scopes and manage tokens used by the agent

name: Code Sandbox Platform Engineers
description: Build and maintain the secure execution environment the agent uses

name: Agent Provider
description: Develop and operate the GitHub agent platform

name: Intellectual Property Rights Holders
description: Owners of copyrighted material possibly referenced or modified

name: Third-Party Integration Vendors
description: Tools connected via webhooks affected by agent commits or PRs

name: Package Registry Operators (npm, PyPI, Maven Central)
description: Receive and distribute releases produced from repos

name: Deployment Platform Owners (Cloud, App Stores)
description: Downstream platforms receiving agent-triggered releases

name: Data Subjects in Repos/Issues
description: Individuals whose personal data may be present in repository content

name: Fork Maintainers
description: Owners of repository forks where the agent might open PRs or sync changes

name: License Compliance Analysts
description: Track third-party license obligations in code authored or modified by the agent
